source: Based on our encouraging results reversing BRAFi resistance in different cell lines, and specifically in Patient #1's ex vivo and in vitro samples, Patient #1 was treated following recurrence on vemurafenib alone with vemurafenib at standard dosing plus 250 mg daily of CQ during focal radiation of large primary lesions.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: Vemurafenib was continued and the chloroquine dose was increased to 500 mg daily following completion of radiation to treat leptomeningeal metastatic disease sites in Patient #1.
source: Vemurafenib was continued and the CQ dose was increased to 500 mg daily following completion of radiation to treat leptomenengeal metastatic disease sites.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: Addition of chloroquine to the continued vemurafenib treatment resulted in clinical improvement and decreased growth of metastatic tumor sites in Patient #1.
source: Consistent with the ex vivo and in vitro tumor modeling, addition of CQ to the continued vemurafenib treatment resulted in clinical improvement and decreased growth of metastatic tumor sites as shown by MRI (Figure 10A–B).
evidence: Clinical observation described in text with reference to figures.

claim: Robust LC3II accumulation in peripheral white blood cells following chloroquine therapy suggests effective autophagy inhibition at the doses of chloroquine used for Patient #1.
source: Robust LC3II accumulation in peripheral white blood cells following CQ therapy (Figure 10C) suggests effective autophagy inhibition at the doses of CQ used for this patient.
evidence: Experimental observation described in text with reference to figure.

claim: A continued favorable response to the combination therapy was maintained for 7 months in Patient #1.
source: In stark contrast with the rapidly growing recurrent metastases, where significant growth was seen after just two weeks at the time of initial relapse, a continued favorable response to the combination therapy was maintained for 7 months.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: Patient #1 had to stop therapy for unrelated medical issues after 7 months.
source: At this time, patient #1 had to stop therapy for unrelated medical issues.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: Patient #6 had a complex medical situation, including extensive multi-focal dural ectasia throughout the CNS.
source: Patient #6 had a complex medical situation, including extensive multi-focal dural ectasia throughout the CNS, resulting in a severe chronic pain disorder and central hypoventilation requiring non-invasive ventilation while sleeping.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: Patient #6 developed an ill-defined expansion of the brainstem with a T2 bright mass of the left anterolateral medulla.
source: This patient developed an ill-defined expansion of the brainstem with a T2 bright mass of the left anterolateral medulla (Figure 10D).
evidence: Clinical case description with reference to figure.

claim: A needle biopsy of the lesion in Patient #6 was diagnostic for a BRAFV600E ganglioglioma.
source: A needle biopsy of this lesion was diagnostic for a BRAFV600E ganglioglioma.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: Patient #6 presented with a worsening left facial palsy, increased difficulty swallowing, and balance deterioration after six months on vemurafenib single drug therapy.
source: Due to the continued presence of tumor mass, she was maintained on vemurafenib single drug therapy for an additional six months when she presented with a worsening left facial (CN VII) palsy, increased difficulty swallowing, and balance deterioration.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: Progressive tumor growth was demonstrated on MRI in Patient #6 associated with worsening clinical symptoms on vemurafenib alone.
source: Associated with these worsening clinical symptoms on vemurafenib alone, progressive tumor growth was demonstrated on MRI (Figure 10E).
evidence: Clinical observation described in text with reference to figure.

claim: Within four weeks of the addition of chloroquine, Patient #6 showed clinical improvement with improved swallowing and CN VII nerve palsy.
source: CQ (500 mg daily) was added as a second agent and she continued on vemurafenib. In contrast with her response to vemurafenib alone, and consistent with the other patients where combined therapy overcame acquired resistance to vemurafenib, within four weeks of the addition of CQ Patient #6 showed clinical improvement with improved swallowing and CN VII nerve palsy.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: Clinical improvement was maintained for two and a half months in Patient #6.
source: This clinical improvement was maintained for two and a half months
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: Patient #6 developed further ventriculoperitoneal shunt failure requiring surgical intervention.
source: when, unfortunately, the patient developed further ventriculoperitoneal shunt failure requiring surgical intervention and her medications were discontinued to allow complete surgical healing.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: Within three weeks of stopping therapy, Patient #6's swallowing difficulties recurred.
source: Within three weeks of stopping therapy, her swallowing difficulties recurred.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: An MRI demonstrated an unchanged size of the brainstem mass in Patient #6 after stopping therapy.
source: An MRI at this time demonstrated an unchanged size of the brainstem mass (Figure 10E).
evidence: Clinical observation described in text with reference to figure.

claim: Both Patient #1 and Patient #6 required a treatment interruption to allow for healing from unrelated medical issues.
source: Both Patient #1 and Patient #6 required a treatment interruption to allow for healing from unrelated medical issues.
evidence: Clinical case description.

claim: In both patients, treatment interruption resulted in significant clinical deterioration.
source: In both patients this resulted in significant clinical deterioration.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: During a six-month treatment interruption, Patient #1 demonstrated progressive radiographic disease with associated clinical decline.
source: For Patient #1, during a six-month treatment interruption, she demonstrated progressive radiographic disease with associated clinical decline and was enrolled in a palliative care program (Figure 11A).
evidence: Clinical observation described in text with reference to figure.

claim: Resistance to BRAF inhibition has been reported to be reversible following a period of treatment interruption in melanoma.
source: Resistance to BRAF inhibition has been reported to be reversible following a period of treatment interruption in melanoma (Seghers et al., 2012)
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A short interval scan done at four weeks demonstrated rapid tumor progression on vemurafenib alone in Patient #1 after treatment interruption.
source: However a short interval scan done at four weeks demonstrated rapid tumor progression on vemurafenib alone (Figure 11B)

claim: Patient #1's tumor retained its previously acquired resistance to the BRAF inhibitor after treatment interruption.
source: indicating that her tumor retained its previously acquired resistance to the BRAF inhibitor.

claim: Combination BRAF inhibition and MEK inhibition prevents MAPK pathway reactivation and an improved reduction in pERK in glioma models.
source: It has also been reported that combination BRAF inhibition and MEK inhibition prevents MAPK pathway reactivation and an improved reduction in pERK in glioma models (Grossauer et al., 2016).

claim: Combination vemurafenib plus trametinib was not well tolerated in Patient #1.
source: A trial of combination vemurafenib plus trametinib was therefore initiated based on these data, but this combination was not well tolerated in this patient.

claim: After an initial stabilization lasting four weeks on trametinib, Patient #1 had further clinical decline with an evolving left hemiparesis and the development of focal seizures.
source: After an initial stabilization lasting four weeks, Patient #1 had further clinical decline with an evolving left hemiparesis and the development of focal seizures.

claim: Imaging repeated two months after the addition of MEK inhibition demonstrated significant tumor growth in Patient #1.
source: Imaging repeated two months after the addition of MEK inhibition demonstrated significant tumor growth (Figure 11C).
evidence: Clinical observation described in text with reference to figure.

claim: At an evaluation four weeks after re-initiation of the combination with autophagy inhibition therapy, Patient #1 reported an overall improvement.
source: In a final attempt to control tumor growth, Patient #1 was restarted on combination vemurafenib and CQ. At an evaluation four weeks after re-initiation of the combination with autophagy inhibition therapy, Patient #1 reported an overall improvement.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: Patient #1 had regained partial use of her left side including the ability to open/close her left hand and move her left arm at the elbow after re-initiation of combination therapy.
source: She had regained partial use of her left side including the ability to open/close her left hand and move her left arm at the elbow.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: Patient #1 had regained the ability to walk unassisted for short distances where she had become wheelchair bound.
source: She had also regained the ability to walk unassisted for short distances where she had become wheelchair bound.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: An MRI demonstrated a measurable reduction in Patient #1's main solid tumor mass four weeks after re-initiation of combination therapy.
source: An MRI at this time demonstrated a measurable reduction in her main solid tumor mass (Figure 11D).
evidence: Clinical observation described in text with reference to figure.

claim: Patient #1 demonstrates the potential risks of cross-resistance and resistance to combination therapies targeting the same pathway.
source: This patient therefore demonstrates the potential risks of cross-resistance and resistance to combination therapies targeting the same pathway.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from clinical case.

claim: Despite a clearly highly resistant tumor, the addition of autophagy inhibition continued to have a clinical benefit in Patient #1.
source: But also showed that despite a clearly highly resistant tumor, the addition of autophagy inhibition continued to have a clinical benefit.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from clinical case.

claim: A recent study by Ahronian et al. evaluated resistance in colorectal cancer and found multiple resistance mechanisms across tumors.
source: A recent study by Ahronian et al. evaluated resistance in colorectal cancer and highlighted many of the difficulties in combatting resistance to BRAFi (Ahronian et al., 2015). They found multiple resistance mechanisms across tumors
evidence: Describes findings from prior study with citation.

claim: Often more than one resistance mechanism exists in a particular patient with colorectal cancer.
source: and often more than one resistance mechanism in a particular patient.
evidence: Describes findings from prior study.

claim: When cells became resistant to one combination of drugs, there was often cross-resistance to other potential combination therapies in colorectal cancer.
source: More importantly, they found that when cells became resistant to one combination of drugs, there was often cross-resistance to other potential combination therapies.
evidence: Describes findings from prior study.

claim: Tumor heterogeneity is a significant concern with studies showing branched evolution in mutations and resistance mechanisms.
source: Tumor heterogeneity is also a significant concern with studies showing branched evolution in mutations and resistance mechanisms that can contribute to acquired resistance.
evidence: Describes findings from prior studies.

claim: Heterogeneity can occur both temporally as well as geographically within the same patient.
source: Such heterogeneity can occur both temporally as well as geographically within the same patient (Shi et al., 2014).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of autophagy with chloroquine can circumvent different molecularly distinct resistance mechanisms.
source: Here we present evidence from cell lines with both experimentally acquired and different molecularly defined resistance mechanisms and from tumor samples from patients with clinically acquired and intrinsic BRAFi resistance, that pharmacological inhibition of autophagy with CQ can achieve this goal.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings.

claim: Genetic inhibition of autophagy can circumvent different molecularly distinct resistance mechanisms.
source: In the cell lines where it was experimentally feasible, we could also demonstrate a similar effect with genetic inhibition of autophagy.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings.

claim: Regardless of the resistance mechanism to the BRAF inhibitor, autophagy inhibition was able to improve the response to BRAF inhibitors.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that regardless of the resistance mechanism to the BRAF inhibitor, autophagy inhibition was able to improve the response to BRAFi.
evidence: Summary conclusion drawn from all experimental data.

claim: Rapid clinical responses (in as little as six weeks) were seen in patients with both high and low-grade tumors with acquired BRAF inhibitor resistance.
source: We have seen rapid clinical responses (in as little as six weeks) in patients with both high and low-grade tumors with acquired BRAFi resistance.
evidence: Summary of clinical observations.

claim: The first clinical responses to combination therapy have been sustained.
source: These first clinical responses have also been sustained.
evidence: Summary of clinical observations.

source: Patient #1 demonstrated control and reduction of her metastatic tumors for greater than seven months

source: whereas she had previously shown MRI-measurable tumor growth in as little as two weeks.

claim: Patient #1 has experienced clinical benefit when the autophagy inhibitor was added to vemurafenib despite having demonstrated subsequent acquisition of clinical resistance to MEK inhibition.
source: Moreover, patient #1 has experienced clinical benefit when the autophagy inhibitor was added to vemurafenib despite having demonstrated subsequent acquisition of clinical resistance to MEK inhibition after the acquisition of BRAF resistance.
evidence: Clinical observation described in text.

claim: The first patient reported by the authors maintained sustained tumor regression on the combination of vemurafenib and chloroquine for more than 2 ½ years without significant clinical complications.
source: Also, the first patient we reported (Levy et al., 2014) maintained sustained tumor regression on the combination of vemurafenib and CQ for more than 2 ½ years without significant clinical complications.
evidence: Clinical observation with citation to prior work.

claim: By targeting autophagy, it may be feasible to overcome kinase inhibitor resistance and re-establish effective tumor control.
source: However, based on our results, we hypothesize that by targeting an entirely different cellular process, i.e. autophagy, upon which these same tumor cells rely, it may be feasible to overcome such resistance and thus re-establish effective tumor control.
evidence: Hypothesis based on experimental and clinical findings.

claim: This strategy can work even when different resistance mechanisms apply.
source: Importantly, our data suggest that this strategy can work even when different resistance mechanisms apply.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data.

claim: This can be done using chloroquine, which is an approved, safe, and inexpensive drug.
source: This can be done using CQ, which is an approved, safe, and inexpensive drug
evidence: Statement about chloroquine properties.

claim: It should be feasible to quickly test this hypothesis in clinical trials in the context of BRAF mutant pediatric brain cancers.
source: Importantly, in the context of BRAF mutant pediatric brain cancers where BRAF inhibition is already being tested, it should be feasible to quickly test this hypothesis in clinical trials.
evidence: Proposal based on findings and current clinical context.
